item.title: Police seek man wanted in theft at Riverhead Target
item.description: Suffolk County Crime Stoppers and Riverhead Town police are asking for the public’s help to identify a man accused of stealing about $300 worth of clothing from Target in Riverhead and fleeing on a black motorcycle.

item.title: Presidents Day: Closings and schedule changes
item.description: Here's a rundown of closings and schedule changes for today's holiday.

item.title: Riverhead woman reported missing identified as woman found dead in Manorville woods: Suffolk police
item.description: Kathleen Harrison Trent, 63, of Riverhead, has been identified as the woman found dead in a wooded area in Manorville on Feb. 11, Suffolk police said.

item.title: Main Road warehouse plan pulled; Stony Brook Ambulance Center hearing reopened; HVAC business proposed at former Buoy One site
item.description: ZBA Feb. 12 meeting wrap: 52 Main Rd. warehouse application pulled, PBMC asks ZBA to reopen hearing on Stony Brook Ambulance Center.

item.title: Helen Jean Elak, 96
item.description: Helen Jean Elak of Riverhead died Feb. 13, 2026, at home. She was 96 years old.

item.title: Dense fog advisory in effect Tuesday night into Wednesday morning
item.description: A dense fog advisory is in effect from 10 p.m. Tuesday through 10 a.m. Wednesday, the National Weather Service said in a statement this afternoon.

item.title: East End Hospice, Suffolk community college launch hospice rotation for paramedic students
item.description: Suffolk paramedic students begin a hospice-specific clinical rotation at East End Hospice’s Kanas Center, a first in New York.

item.title: Cannabis law change clarifies buffer measurements near schools, houses of worship
item.description: A new law sets a door-to-door standard for measuring minimum distances required near schools, houses of worship.

item.title: Fire suppression system accidentally discharged at Riverhead gas station Wednesday morning
item.description: The fire suppression system at BJ’s gas station in Riverhead was accidentally activated this morning, coating customers, vehicles and much of the site with a dry chemical agent that’s used to extinguish fuel-related and electrical fires

item.title: State DEC warns against contact with dead or sick birds on Long Island
item.description: The State DEC is warning the public against contact with dead or sick birds, after receiving “numerous reports of dead or sick waterfowl throughout Long Island… and along the Peconic Bay.”
